title: A heavier central body
hook: Change central mass and predict circular-orbit speed.
misconception: circular-orbit speed doubles when central mass doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply v = √(GM/r) to compare circular-orbit speed when central mass changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a circular Newtonian orbit at fixed radius around a dominant spherical mass, v = √(GM/r). When central mass doubles, circular-orbit speed becomes √2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model v = √(GM/r); scaling exponent 0.5. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a circular Newtonian orbit at fixed radius around a dominant spherical mass, with a nonzero initial result. If central mass triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on circular-orbit speed?
recall.why: Apply v = √(GM/r) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is √3.
